p.src: Now Clear Breeze Mountain lay not far from Qingzhou, only a little over a hundred li away. Clear Breeze Stockade stood at the three-way crossroads outside Qingzhou, in a place called Clear Breeze Town. Since the three roads led to three mountains infested with outlaws, Clear Breeze Stockade had been specially established there in Clear Breeze Town. The place held three to five thousand households and was only a little more than one stage from Clear Breeze Mountain. That day, the three chiefs returned to the mountain.

p.src: As for Song Gongming, he went on alone with several bundles on his back until he reached Clear Breeze Town, where he asked the way to Commandant Hua's residence. A townsman replied, “The offices of Clear Breeze Stockade stand in the middle of the market town. The small compound to the south is the residence of Civil Commandant Liu; the small compound to the north is the residence of Military Commandant Hua.” When Song Jiang heard this, he thanked the man and made for the northern compound. At the gate he saw several soldiers standing guard. They asked his name, then went inside to announce him. Presently a young officer hurried out of the stockade, seized Song Jiang by the arm, and bowed before him. And what manner of man was he? Behold:

p.src: White teeth, red lips, and handsome eyes; Two clear brows sweeping into his temples; A slender waist, broad shoulders, and the build of an ape. He could ride the fiercest horse And loved to fly the eastern sea hawk. At a hundred paces he pierced the willow leaf, so mighty was his wondrous arm; His drawn bow shone clear as the autumn moon, And his feathered shafts flew like bursting stars of frost. Men called him “Little Li Guang”; A scion of warriors—Hua Rong.

p.src: His battle robe was embroidered in gold and kingfisher green; At his waist, a jade belt was inlaid with mountain-rhinoceros horn. A dark blue kerchief and cap bore two small rings; His civil-and-military boots were trimmed low in green.

p.src: After Hua Rong had bowed to Song Jiang, he shouted for the soldiers to take his bundles, cudgel-sword, and waist sword. Supporting Song Jiang, he led him straight into the main hall and invited him to sit in the central seat upon the couch. Hua Rong then bowed four more times with his head to the floor. Rising, he said, “It has already been five or six years since I parted from my elder brother, and I have thought of you constantly. I heard that you killed a vile harlot and that the authorities sent warrants everywhere for your arrest. When I learned of it, I felt as though seated on a bed of needles. I wrote more than ten letters in succession to your honored manor asking for news. Did any of them reach you? By Heaven's grace you have come here today, and I am fortunate enough to see you again. It is the greatest comfort of my life.” With that, he bowed again. Song Jiang took hold of him and said, “Worthy brother, do not stand so much on ceremony. Sit down and hear what I have to tell you.” Hua Rong sat respectfully to one side. Song Jiang then related in detail the whole story: how he had killed Yan Poxi, sought refuge with the great lord Chai, met Wu Song at Squire Kong's manor, been captured on Clear Breeze Mountain, and encountered Yan Shun, among all the other events. When Hua Rong had heard him out, he replied, “Elder brother, you have endured so many hardships. Now that you have fortunately come here, stay for several years, and we shall consider what to do afterward.” Song Jiang said, “Even if my younger brother Song Qing had not sent a letter to Squire Kong's manor, I had intended to make a special journey here to visit you.” Hua Rong invited Song Jiang into the rear hall and summoned his wife, née Cui, to come and bow to her husband's elder brother. After she had bowed, Hua Rong also called out his younger sister to pay respects to Song Jiang. He then had Song Jiang change his clothes, shoes, and stockings and bathe in fragrant hot water, while a banquet was prepared in the rear hall to wash away the dust of his journey.

p.src: At the banquet that day, Song Jiang told Hua Rong in full detail how he had rescued Commandant Liu's wife. Hua Rong frowned upon hearing it and said, “Elder brother, why ever did you rescue that woman for no reason? It would have been just as well to silence that scoundrel's household for good!” Song Jiang said, “That is a strange thing to say! I heard she was the wife of a commandant of Clear Breeze Stockade, so for the sake of your colleague I insisted on rescuing her from the mountain, even at the risk of offending Wang the Short. Why do you speak in this way?” Hua Rong said, “Elder brother, you do not know. I do not say this to boast, but Clear Breeze Stockade is a vital position for Qingzhou. If I alone had continued guarding this place, how would the outlaws near and far have dared throw Qingzhou into utter disorder? Recently they appointed that penniless, pedantic sourpuss as chief commandant. The scoundrel is a civil official with no ability at all. Since taking office, he has extorted what few well-to-do households there are in the countryside, perverted the law, and stopped at nothing. I am the deputy commandant, a military officer, yet that fellow constantly provokes me. I could gladly kill that corrupt, filthy thieving beast. Why, elder brother, did you rescue that scoundrel's wife? Worse still, that woman is utterly wicked. She does nothing but incite her husband to cruelty—harming innocent people and coveting bribes. It would have served the wretch right to suffer some dishonor. You mistakenly saved a person of such worthless character.” When Song Jiang heard this, he admonished him: “Worthy brother, you are mistaken! As the old saying goes, ‘Enmity should be resolved, not created.’ He is your fellow official. Though he has faults, you should conceal his failings and proclaim his virtues. Worthy brother, do not take so narrow a view.” Hua Rong said, “Elder brother, your insight is perfectly clear. Tomorrow, when I see Commandant Liu at the public offices, I shall tell him how you rescued his wife.” Song Jiang said, “If you do so, it will show your own magnanimity as well.” Hua Rong, his wife, and the rest of his household attended Song Jiang morning and evening with the utmost care, offering him wine and serving him food. That night they prepared a bed and curtains beneath the veranda of the rear hall and invited Song Jiang to rest there. The next day they again prepared wine, food, and a banquet to entertain him. Let us spare the tedious details. After arriving at Hua Rong's stockade, Song Jiang spent four or five days feasting and drinking. Hua Rong had several trusted retainers. Each day a different one was assigned to carry some small pieces of silver and accompany Song Jiang about Clear Breeze Town, where he could watch the bustle of the marketplace and visit the villages, Daoist temples, and Buddhist monasteries, strolling at leisure for his pleasure. From that day onward, one of these trusted men accompanied him on his rambles and invited him to amuse himself in the marketplace. Clear Breeze Town also had several small entertainment booths, as well as teahouses and wineshops, all of which goes without saying. That day Song Jiang and the trusted retainer watched the entertainment for a while in one of the small booths, then toured a Buddhist monastery and a Daoist temple in a nearby village, after which the man invited him to drink at a wineshop in town. When they were about to leave, the retainer took out silver to pay the bill. But Song Jiang would by no means let him pay and instead took out his own small silver and settled the account. When Song Jiang returned, he said nothing of it to Hua Rong. The man who had drunk with him was delighted: he kept his silver and gained a day of leisure besides. From then on, one man was assigned each day to accompany Song Jiang on his rambles. And every day it was Song Jiang alone who spent the money. Since his arrival at the stockade, there was not one person who did not respect and love him. Song Jiang had stayed at Hua Rong's stockade for nearly a month. The last winter month was drawing to an end, spring was returning, and the Lantern Festival was already near.

p.src: Now the residents of Clear Breeze Stockade township discussed the matter of displaying lanterns and made ready to celebrate the Lantern Festival. They levied money and goods, then erected a small lantern mountain before the Temple of the Lord of the Soil, decking it with colored silk and flowers and hanging five or six hundred bowl-shaped lanterns upon it. Inside the temple, every kind of festival entertainment competed for attention. Before every house a lantern awning was raised, each household vying to make its lights the finest. The town offered trades and entertainments of every description. Though it could not compare with the imperial capital, even this seemed like heaven on earth. At that time Song Jiang was drinking with Hua Rong in the stockade, and the Lantern Festival had arrived. The day was beautifully clear. Around the fourth watch of the morning, Hua Rong mounted his horse, rode to the public offices, and mustered several hundred soldiers, ordering them to keep order in the town that evening. He also assigned many other soldiers to divide into groups and guard the stockade gates on every side. Around the eighth watch of the day he returned to the stockade and invited Song Jiang to take some refreshments. Song Jiang said to Hua Rong, “I hear that lanterns will be lit throughout the town tonight. I should like to go and see them.” Hua Rong replied, “I had intended to accompany you, elder brother, but my official duties prevent me from strolling there at leisure with you. Tonight, take two or three men of my household with you to view the lanterns, and return early. I shall await you at home with a modest family feast and three cups of wine to celebrate the festival.” “Excellent,” said Song Jiang. Soon evening drew on, and the bright moon pushed its way up from the east. Indeed:

p.src: Water clock and bronze clepsydra, do not hasten the hours; starry bridges and fiery trees stand radiant through the night. The lantern mountain towers into the azure clouds—what reveler would not come to see it!

p.src: That evening Song Jiang set out with two or three trusted members of Hua Rong’s household, who attended him as they strolled along at an easy pace. When they reached Clear Breeze township to view the lanterns, they saw awnings erected before every house and ornamental lanterns hanging everywhere. Many stories were painted upon them; there were also peony lanterns cut from colored silk with white patterns, as well as extraordinary hibiscus and lotus lanterns. The four or five of them linked hands and came to the Temple of the Lord of the Soil. When they looked upon the little lantern mountain, they beheld:

p.src: Through mountain crags twin dragons sported in the water; amid rosy clouds a solitary crane soared toward heaven. Golden lotus lanterns and jade plum lanterns shimmered like a vast expanse of crystal; Lotus lanterns and hibiscus lanterns spread a thousand clusters of brocade. Silver moth ornaments vied in brilliance, paired beside embroidered ribbons and scented balls; Snow-willow ornaments competed in splendor, their strands brushing gorgeous kingfisher-feathered banners and curtains. Village songs and festival drums clamored amid the shadows of the lanterns; Weaving women and silkworm tenders enjoyed the sights together in the glow of painted candles. Though no beauties sang songs of love, all celebrated the abundant harvest of a bountiful year.

p.src: Song Jiang and his three companions watched for a while before the lantern mountain, then gradually made their way south. After no more than five or seven hundred paces, they saw lanterns and candles blazing ahead, where a crowd had gathered merrily before the gate of a large walled compound. Whenever the gong sounded, the crowd burst into cheers. Looking closer, Song Jiang saw that a troupe was performing the Baolao dance. Song Jiang was short and could see nothing from behind the crowd. One of the trusted attendants accompanying him knew members of the festival troupe, so he had the crowd part and make way for Song Jiang to watch. The Baolao dancer twisted his body in a comically rustic fashion, and at the sight Song Jiang laughed heartily.

One of the trusted attendants accompanying him knew members of the festival troupe, so he had the crowd part and make way for Song Jiang to watch.
The Baolao dancer twisted his body in a comically rustic fashion, and at the sight Song Jiang laughed heartily.

p.src: Inside the compound, Commander Liu and his wife were watching with their two sons and several women servants. Hearing Song Jiang’s laughter, Commander Liu’s wife recognized him in the lantern light. Pointing him out to her husband, she said, “That short black fellow there is the bandit chief who abducted me on Clear Breeze Mountain the other day.” Commander Liu was startled to hear this. He summoned six or seven personal attendants and ordered them to seize the black fellow who had laughed. Song Jiang heard the order, turned, and fled. Before he had passed more than a dozen houses, the soldiers overtook and seized him, like a black eagle pursuing a purple swallow, or a fierce tiger devouring a lamb. They took him into the stockade, bound him with four hempen ropes, and escorted him before the hall. When the three trusted attendants saw Song Jiang taken away, they ran back to inform Hua Rong.

p.src: Now Commander Liu sat in the hall and ordered the prisoner brought before him. The men crowded around Song Jiang and forced him to his knees before the hall. Commander Liu shouted, “You are a murderous brigand who plunders on Clear Breeze Mountain. How dare you come here openly to view the lanterns! Now that you have been captured, what have you to say for yourself?” Song Jiang pleaded, “I am Zhang San, a traveler from Yuncheng County, and an old friend of Commander Hua. I have been here for many days and have never committed robbery on Clear Breeze Mountain.” Commander Liu’s wife emerged from behind a screen and cried, “You rogue, you still deny it! Do you remember making me address you as Great King?” Song Jiang pleaded, “My lady, you are mistaken. Did I not tell you then, ‘I too am a traveler from Yuncheng County. I was abducted and held here and could not get down from the mountain’?” Commander Liu said, “If you were a traveler held captive there, how did you manage to descend the mountain today and come here to view the lanterns?” The woman said, “When you were on the mountain, you sat brazenly in the central chair while I addressed you as Great King, and you paid no attention to me!” Song Jiang said, “My lady, have you entirely forgotten that I did everything in my power to rescue you and send you down the mountain? Why do you now insist on making a bandit of me?” The woman flew into a rage at this. Pointing at Song Jiang, she cursed, “A shameless liar through and through! How will he ever confess unless he is beaten?” “You are right,” said Commander Liu. He shouted for the bamboo cudgels to be brought and ordered the rogue beaten. They gave him two successive rounds of blows, beating Song Jiang until his flesh split open and fresh blood streamed forth. Commander Liu then ordered him shackled in irons. The next day they were to prepare a prison cart and escort Zhang San, the “Tiger of Yuncheng,” to the prefectural seat.

p.src: —Hua Rong respectfully addresses his esteemed colleague: My humble kinsman, Master Liu, recently arrived from Jizhou. While viewing the lanterns he inadvertently offended your honored authority. I earnestly beg you, for friendship’s sake, to pardon and release him, and I shall call upon you personally to offer my thanks. Forgive the disrespect of this hastily written note. I beg your kind consideration. There is no more to say.

p.src: Liu Gao read the letter and flew into a rage. Tearing it to shreds, he cursed, “That scoundrel Hua Rong has some nerve! You are an official appointed by the imperial court, yet you conspire with a vicious outlaw and try to deceive me as well. This rogue has already confessed that he is Zhang San of Yuncheng County. How dare you write that he is an elder named Liu? I am not one for you to make a fool of. You gave him the surname Liu, the same as mine, thinking that would make me release him!” He shouted an order for his men to shove the messenger out. Driven out through the stockade gate, the attendant hurried back and reported everything to Hua Rong. When Hua Rong heard this, he cried, “My poor brother! Quickly, saddle my horse!” Hua Rong donned his armor, secured his bow and arrows, seized his spear, and mounted. Taking thirty or fifty soldiers, all armed with spears and staves, he raced straight to Liu Gao’s stockade. When the gate guards saw him, how could they dare bar his way? Seeing the menace in Hua Rong’s bearing, they were all terrified and scattered in every direction. Hua Rong charged up to the hall, dismounted with spear in hand, and arrayed his thirty or fifty men before it. Hua Rong called out, “Commandant Liu, come out and speak with me.” Hearing him, Liu Gao was frightened out of his wits. Knowing that Hua Rong was a military officer, he did not dare come out to face him. When Liu Gao failed to appear, Hua Rong waited a while, then ordered his men to search the side rooms on either side. When the thirty or fifty soldiers searched together, they soon found Song Jiang in a side room off the gallery. He had been hoisted high from a roof beam with hemp rope, bound in iron chains, and beaten until the flesh on both legs had split open. Several soldiers cut the ropes, broke open the iron fetters, and rescued Song Jiang. Hua Rong ordered the soldiers to take him home first. Then Hua Rong mounted, leveled his spear in his hand, and called out, “Commandant Liu, you may be the senior commandant, but what can you do to Hua Rong? Who has no kinsmen? What did you mean by this? You seized a cousin of mine in his own lodging and forcibly branded him an outlaw. You are a fine bully indeed! Tomorrow I shall settle this with you.” Hua Rong led his men back to his own stockade to see how Song Jiang was faring.

p.src: Now when Commandant Liu saw Hua Rong rescue the prisoner and take him away, he hurriedly mustered one or two hundred men and ordered them to go to Hua Rong’s stockade and recapture him. Among those two hundred men were two newly appointed drill instructors. The chief instructor had some skill with spear and saber, but his prowess was far inferior to Hua Rong’s. Yet he dared not disobey Liu Gao, so he had no choice but to lead the men toward Hua Rong’s stockade. The soldiers guarding the gate went in and reported this to Hua Rong. The sky was not yet fully light. The two hundred or so men crowded before the gate, but none dared enter first, for all feared Hua Rong’s prowess. As the sky gradually brightened, they saw that the two great gates stood open. Commandant Hua sat in the main hall, holding a bow in his left hand and an arrow in his right. The men remained packed before the gate. Hua Rong raised his bow and shouted, “You soldiers ought to know that every grievance has its true offender and every debt its rightful debtor. Liu Gao sent you here, but do not risk yourselves trying to distinguish yourselves on his behalf. Those two newly appointed instructors of yours have not yet witnessed Commandant Hua’s skill. Today I shall first show you all my archery; afterward, any of you scoundrels who still wish to distinguish yourselves for Liu Gao may enter if you are unafraid. Watch me first shoot the head of the mace held by the door god painted on the left gate!” He nocked an arrow, drew the bow to its full, and with a single shot cried, “Strike!” The arrow struck squarely in the head of the door god’s mace. At the sight, everyone gasped in astonishment. Hua Rong took a second arrow and called, “Now watch my second shot. I shall hit the scarlet tassel on the helmet of the door god on the right.” Another arrow whistled forth, neither to one side nor the other, and struck the tip of the tassel dead center. The two arrows now stood fixed in the two gate leaves. Hua Rong took up a third arrow and shouted, “Now watch my third shot. I mean to strike the white-clad instructor in the heart.” The man cried, “Aiyaa!” He wheeled about and was the first to flee. The others raised a clamor and all fled together. Hua Rong ordered the stockade gate closed, then went to the rear hall to attend to Song Jiang. Hua Rong said, “It was my fault, brother, that you suffered such torment.” Song Jiang replied, “I shall be all right. I only fear that scoundrel Liu Gao will not let the matter rest with you. We must devise a sound plan for the future.” Hua Rong said, “I am prepared to cast away this official commission and settle matters with that scoundrel.” Song Jiang said, “Who would have thought that woman would repay kindness with enmity and have her husband give me such a beating? I had meant to reveal my true name, but I feared the affair of Yan Poxi might come to light, so I merely called myself Zhang San, a traveler from Yuncheng. But that insolent Liu Gao meant to pass me off as Zhang San, the ‘Yuncheng Tiger,’ send me under guard to the prefecture, and shut me in a prison cart. Once they branded me a chieftain of the Qingfeng Mountain bandits, I would be hacked to pieces in no time. Had you not come in person to rescue me with all your strength, even lips of bronze and a tongue of iron could never have argued me free.” Hua Rong said, “I thought that, being a man of letters, he would surely respect the kinship of a shared surname. That was why I wrote ‘Elder Liu.’ I never imagined he could be so utterly devoid of human feeling. Now that I have rescued you and brought you home, we shall deal with whatever comes.” Song Jiang said, “You are mistaken, good brother. Since you relied on your bold might to rescue me, we must now think thrice before doing anything further. As the old saying goes, ‘Guard against choking when you eat, and against stumbling when you walk.’ You openly snatched his prisoner away. He hastily sent men to seize me back, only for you to frighten them into scattering. How could he possibly let the matter end there? He is certain to lodge an official complaint against you. Tonight I shall go up to Qingfeng Mountain and hide. Tomorrow you can deny everything to his face, and in the end it will amount only to a lawsuit over a brawl caused by discord between civil and military officers. If he seizes me again, you will no longer be able to argue the matter out with him.” Hua Rong said, “I am only a rash fighting man and lack your wise foresight, elder brother.

p.src: Now Liu Gao, the commandant of the civil stronghold, saw his soldiers straggling back to the fort one after another, saying, “Commandant Hua is extraordinarily brave and formidable. Who would dare go near and face his bow and arrows?” The two instructors said, “One shot from him would pierce a clean hole straight through a man. None of us can go.” That scoundrel Liu Gao was, after all, a civil official; subtle and ruthless, he had schemes of his own. Liu Gao considered the matter: “Now that Hua Rong has seized him back, he will surely release him during the night and send him up Mount Qingfeng, then come tomorrow and brazenly deny everything to my face. Even if the quarrel were taken before our superiors, it would be treated merely as a brawl arising from discord between civil and military officers. How, then, could I do anything to him? Tonight I shall send twenty or thirty soldiers to lie in wait five li down the road. If fortune favors us and they catch him, I shall have him brought here and secretly imprisoned in my house. Then I shall send someone through the night to report to the prefecture and ask its military officers to come and take custody of him. They can arrest Hua Rong at the same time and put them both to death. Then I alone shall rule Qingfeng Fort and no longer have to endure the insolence of those scoundrels.” That evening he selected more than twenty men. Each took a spear or staff, and they set out under cover of night. At about the second watch, the soldiers returned with Song Jiang’s arms pinioned behind his back. Commandant Liu was overjoyed at the sight and said, “It has turned out exactly as I expected. For now, imprison him in the rear courtyard, and let no one learn of it.” That very night he wrote a sealed official report and sent two trusted retainers racing through the night to deliver the urgent news to Qingzhou Prefecture. The next day, Hua Rong assumed that Song Jiang had gone up Mount Qingfeng. He remained calmly at home, thinking, “I shall wait and see what he does!” He paid the matter no further attention. Liu Gao likewise pretended to know nothing, and neither side said a word about the matter.

p.src: Now the prefect of Qingzhou was just then seated in the public hall conducting official business. The prefect bore the compound surname Murong and the given name Yanda. He was the elder brother of Consort Murong, favorite of the present sovereign, Emperor Huizong. Relying on his sister’s influence, he tyrannized Qingzhou, persecuted innocent people, deceived his fellow officials, and shrank from no evil. Just as he was about to withdraw to his private quarters for breakfast, the constables at his side brought forward Commandant Liu’s report, urgently announcing a case involving bandits. The prefect took it and, after reading Liu Gao’s document, started in alarm. “Hua Rong is the son of a meritorious minister,” he said. “How could he have allied himself with the powerful bandits of Mount Qingfeng? This is no minor offense, but it is not yet clear whether the charge is true.” He ordered the military commandant of the prefecture summoned to the hall and gave him his instructions. This military commandant’s surname was Huang and his given name was Xin. Because he was highly skilled in the martial arts and his might overawed all Qingzhou, he was known as “Guardian of the Three Mountains.” Within the territory administered by Qingzhou stood three notorious mountains: first Mount Qingfeng, second Mount Erlong, and third Mount Taohua. All three were haunts of brigands and outlaws. Huang Xin boasted that he would capture every last man on all three mountains, and for that reason was called “Guardian of the Three Mountains.” Huang Xin, the military commandant, came to the hall and received the prefect’s orders. After leaving, he mustered fifty sturdy soldiers and had them don armor. Then, mounted on his horse and holding aloft his Death’s-Door Sword, he traveled through the night to Qingfeng Fort, rode straight to Liu Gao’s stronghold, and dismounted before its gate. Commandant Liu came out to meet him and invited him into the rear hall, where they exchanged the customary courtesies. On the one hand, he had food and wine prepared for his guest; on the other, he rewarded and feasted the soldiers. Then Song Jiang was brought out from the back for Huang Xin to inspect. Huang Xin said, “There is no need to question this fellow. Build a prison cart tonight and put the scoundrel inside.” They bound a strip of red silk around his head and stuck there a paper banner bearing the words: “Zhang San, the Yuncheng Tiger, Chief Bandit of Mount Qingfeng.” Song Jiang dared not argue and had no choice but to submit to their arrangements. Huang Xin then asked Liu Gao, “When you captured Zhang San, did Hua Rong know about it or not?” Liu Gao replied, “Your humble officer captured him at the second watch last night and secretly hid him in my house. Hua Rong believes that he has gone away and is sitting comfortably at home.” Huang Xin said, “If that is so, the matter will be easy. Tomorrow morning, prepare a gift of mutton and wine and set out a feast in the public hall of the main stronghold. Then conceal thirty or fifty men all around it, ready for action. I shall go to Hua Rong’s house in person and invite him here, claiming, ‘Prefect Murong has heard of the discord between you civil and military officers, and has therefore specially sent me to arrange a feast and reconcile you.’ Once I have lured him into the public hall, watch for me to dash down my wine cup as the signal. Then seize him, and we shall escort both prisoners together to the prefectural seat. What do you think of this plan?” Liu Gao applauded and said, “Your Excellency’s wisdom is indeed superior. It is a brilliant plan. It is truly like ‘catching a turtle in a jar—reaching in and taking it with ease.’”

p.src: That night they settled their plan. At dawn the next day, soldiers were secretly posted beforehand behind the curtains on both sides of the main stockade, while a banquet of wine and food was laid out in the hall as a decoy. Around breakfast time, Huang Xin mounted his horse and, taking only two or three attendants, came to the gate of Hua Rong's stockade. A soldier went in to report his arrival, and Hua Rong asked, “What has he come for?” The soldier replied, “All I heard was that Commandant Huang had come especially to call on you.” On hearing this, Hua Rong went out to welcome him. Huang Xin dismounted, and Hua Rong invited him into the hall. After they had exchanged courtesies, Hua Rong asked, “What official business brings Your Excellency here?” Huang Xin said, “The prefect summoned me and instructed me that, since the civil and military officers of your Qingfeng Stockade are at odds for reasons yet unknown, he sincerely fears that a private feud between you two may hinder public affairs. He has therefore specially sent me with mutton and wine to reconcile you both. Everything has already been prepared in the public hall of the main stockade, so please mount your horse and come with me.” Hua Rong laughed and said, “How would I, Hua Rong, dare deceive Liu Gao? He too is a rightful commandant of the stockade. It is only that he has repeatedly tried to find fault with me. I never imagined this would trouble the prefect and bring you, Commandant, down to our humble stockade. How can I ever repay you?” Huang Xin leaned close to his ear and whispered, “The prefect is concerned only for you. If fighting should break out, what use could that civil official be? You need only follow my lead.” Hua Rong said, “I am deeply grateful for your kindness, Commandant.” Huang Xin then invited Hua Rong to go out through the gate and mount his horse with him. Hua Rong said, “Please stay for just three cups before we go.” Huang Xin replied, “Once matters have been talked through, we may drink our fill.” Hua Rong had no choice but to order his horse prepared. The two rode side by side straight to the main stockade. After they dismounted, Huang Xin took Hua Rong by the hand and led him into the public hall, where they found Liu Gao already waiting. The three men exchanged greetings. Huang Xin called for wine. Meanwhile, his attendants had already led Hua Rong's horse away and shut the stockade gate. Hua Rong knew nothing of the plot. He thought only that Huang Xin was a military officer like himself and surely harbored no evil intent. Huang Xin raised a cup of wine and first offered it to Liu Gao, saying, “The prefect was deeply troubled to hear that you two officers, one civil and one military, were not on good terms despite being colleagues. Today he has specially commissioned me, Huang Xin, to come and mediate between you gentlemen. I ask that you place service to the court above all else, and hereafter discuss every matter together in harmony.” Liu Gao replied, “Though I, Liu Gao, possess little talent, I do understand something of reason and the law. I am ashamed to have caused our gracious prefect such concern. There has been no real quarrel between us. These are merely wild rumors spread by outsiders.” Huang Xin laughed heartily and cried, “Excellent!” After Liu Gao had drunk, Huang Xin poured a second cup and offered it to Hua Rong, saying, “Since Commandant Liu has spoken thus, it must indeed have been idle men spreading false rumors. That being so, please drink a cup.” Hua Rong took the cup and drank. Liu Gao took another cup from the wine service, filled it, and offered it in return to Huang Xin, saying, “You have taken the trouble to honor our humble place with your presence, Commandant. Please drain this cup.” Huang Xin accepted the wine and held the cup in his hand. Glancing all around, he saw more than ten soldiers crowding into the hall. Huang Xin dashed the cup to the floor. At once a shout rose from the rear hall, and thirty or fifty sturdy soldiers rushed from behind the curtains on both sides, swarmed upon Hua Rong, and threw him down before the hall. Huang Xin shouted, “Bind him!” Hua Rong cried out repeatedly, “What crime have I committed?” Huang Xin laughed loudly and bellowed, “You still dare to protest! You have conspired with the bandits of Qingfeng Mountain and joined them in rebellion against the court. What punishment do you think that deserves? For the sake of our former acquaintance, I refrained from alarming your household and arresting your whole family.”

The two rode side by side straight to the main stockade. After they dismounted, Huang Xin took Hua Rong by the hand and led him into the public hall, where they found Liu Gao already waiting.
The three men exchanged greetings.
Huang Xin called for wine. Meanwhile, his attendants had already led Hua Rong's horse away and shut the stockade gate.
Hua Rong knew nothing of the plot. He thought only that Huang Xin was a military officer like himself and surely harbored no evil intent.

Huang Xin raised a cup of wine and first offered it to Liu Gao, saying, “The prefect was deeply troubled to hear that you two officers, one civil and one military, were not on good terms despite being colleagues. Today he has specially commissioned me, Huang Xin, to come and mediate between you gentlemen.
I ask that you place service to the court above all else, and hereafter discuss every matter together in harmony.”
Liu Gao replied, “Though I, Liu Gao, possess little talent, I do understand something of reason and the law. I am ashamed to have caused our gracious prefect such concern.
There has been no real quarrel between us. These are merely wild rumors spread by outsiders.”
Huang Xin laughed heartily and cried, “Excellent!”

After Liu Gao had drunk, Huang Xin poured a second cup and offered it to Hua Rong, saying, “Since Commandant Liu has spoken thus, it must indeed have been idle men spreading false rumors. That being so, please drink a cup.”
Hua Rong took the cup and drank.

Liu Gao took another cup from the wine service, filled it, and offered it in return to Huang Xin, saying, “You have taken the trouble to honor our humble place with your presence, Commandant. Please drain this cup.”
Huang Xin accepted the wine and held the cup in his hand. Glancing all around, he saw more than ten soldiers crowding into the hall.

Huang Xin dashed the cup to the floor. At once a shout rose from the rear hall, and thirty or fifty sturdy soldiers rushed from behind the curtains on both sides, swarmed upon Hua Rong, and threw him down before the hall.
Huang Xin shouted, “Bind him!”
Hua Rong cried out repeatedly, “What crime have I committed?”
Huang Xin laughed loudly and bellowed, “You still dare to protest!
You have conspired with the bandits of Qingfeng Mountain and joined them in rebellion against the court. What punishment do you think that deserves?
For the sake of our former acquaintance, I refrained from alarming your household and arresting your whole family.”

p.src: it was none other than Song Jiang. Their eyes widened and their mouths fell open. They stared at each other, unable to utter a word. Huang Xin shouted, “This has nothing to do with me. His accuser, Liu Gao, is right here.” Hua Rong said, “No matter, no matter. This man is my kinsman. He is a native of Yuncheng County. If you insist on twisting the facts and calling him a bandit, we shall have our chance to argue the case before the higher authorities.” Huang Xin said, “Since that is what you say, I shall merely escort you to the prefectural seat, where you may argue your own case.” He then ordered Commandant Liu to muster one hundred stockade troops as an escort. Hua Rong then said to Huang Xin, “Commandant, you tricked me into coming here and have arrested me, but even before the imperial court I shall still have a case to argue against him. In consideration of the fact that you and I both hold military office, do not strip off my official clothes, but allow me to sit in the prison cart as I am.” Huang Xin said, “That is easily done. Indeed: When trouble breeds more trouble, show its maker no mercy; when a man harms others and they harm him, let him not complain.
